reason: API and execution workers exited on the first failed heartbeat when PostgreSQL refused or reset connections, though their 30 s leases were still valid; the execution lease watcher fenced the project on any SQL error (wedging it if the heartbeat kept renewing), each streamed chat frame failed on the first lost connection, and the memory reconciler and chat schedule loop died on one failed read. Workers now keep a local monotonic lease bound (LeaseRenewal: last acknowledged renewal start + LEASE_MS - LEASE_SAFETY_MS); inside it the heartbeat retries transient SQL errors (runtime_worker.keep_lease), worker sessions wait to bind a connection before any statement (Database.ride_out_outages, opt-in), the watcher and prepared-restoration wait do not fence, and stream publication retries under the same batch key; past the bound the worker stops with LeaseLost as before, and a definite LeaseLost or SQL answer still stops it at once. Selected: the new outage suite (keeper bound, session wait, real heartbeat on SQLite/PostgreSQL that never resurrects an expired lease); the execution worker suite with the new watcher regression; the worker features suite with the in-process run_worker regression; the memory recovery suite with the loop regression; the journal retry regression and the chat stream cases that pass on main; the coordination, async database/PostgreSQL/auxiliary database, API worker composition, write-lock, runtime memory recovery and diagnostic boundary suites that exercise Database.session, heartbeats and the lease watcher.

Process-level suites (test_execution_worker_process.py) are not selected: they spawn whole Cores and are dominated by host-load readiness here. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. Real-Core evidence (scratch supervisor PostgreSQL Cores on origin/main and on this branch behind a TCP proxy whose listener was stopped and sockets reset, 12-13 s and 45 s outages during a slow streaming chat) is in the PR, not executed by CI.
